items.summary: Continue the four existing SearchWoot launch-readiness evidence tasks; 0 of 4 are closed. Keep the product private and permission outreach unsent. Next evidence action is the consolidated rights, data-flow, consent, vendor, retention, and incident bundle.

Risk disposition: blocked for public launch, rights-dependent monetization, and security-sensitive release; conditional for ordinary reversible growth within existing consent, disclosure, provenance, claims, copyright/trademark, platform-policy, age-sensitive, and data-handling boundaries. Exact decision: retain searchwoot.com private, keep permission outreach unsent, and continue only existing read-only evidence work. Evidence: Woot documentation establishes access mechanics but not commercial/public redistribution rights; Woot terms restrict collection, reuse, and derivative use; accuracy/freshness, measurement/attribution, and security gates remain blocked; compliance is technical-only with 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown. Human counsel is required for Woot rights, jurisdictional privacy/consent treatment, and future affiliate or advertising use. Incomplete telemetry alone does not block ordinary reversible growth.

Launch-readiness tracking remains active: 0 of 4 tasks closed and 4 open. No task is closable on current evidence. Existing progress is limited to official Woot documentation and terms, repository/configuration artifacts, privacy policy, and cookie policy. Next evidence action: attach and review one consolidated read-only bundle and field-level rights matrix covering provenance, permitted storage/caching/display/derivatives, alerts, attribution, freshness, correction, takedown, identifiers, retention, deletion, access, notification consent, unsubscribe behavior, GA4 settings, log fields, vendor coverage, and incident/request procedures.

Data-use review: Woot API deal and price-history data is counsel_required. Missing evidence: written permission or API agreement; field-level provenance and rights; permitted storage, caching, display, derivatives, alerts, attribution, freshness, correction, takedown, trademark, image, price, affiliate, and advertising terms. Smallest next action: complete the field-level rights matrix and route the unsent permission package for human-counsel review.

Data-use review: user alert rules and sync results are evidence_needed. Missing evidence: data inventory, retention, deletion, correction, access, processor terms, notification consent, and unsubscribe behavior. Smallest next action: produce the repository and deployed data-flow and retention table; do not expand notifications.

Data-use review: GA4 analytics is evidence_needed. Missing evidence: deployed consent and withdrawal behavior, GA4 property and data-sharing settings, retention settings, and jurisdictional treatment. Smallest next action: capture existing consent and GA4 configuration without enabling tracking or advertising.

Data-use review: operational logs and Cloudflare hosting data are evidence_needed. Missing evidence: log-field inventory, retention and access controls, vendor/DPA review, incident handling, and data-request procedures. Smallest next action: produce a read-only operator/vendor inventory and identify counsel-required gaps.

Site-specific decision: retain complicated.work parked until banner, consent accept/reject, and GA4 failures are remediated. Retain deadlymaracas.com parked until DNS reachability and a concrete compliance checklist are evidenced. Do not infer audience, revenue, compliance, or launch readiness from missing telemetry.

Revenue and data-quality disposition: preserve the $4.92 Amazon commission for 2026-09-21 as aggregate unattributed revenue. Do not claim site revenue, ROI, margin, payback, budget capacity, cost-to-learn, or causal lift. Analytics is yellow because permissions or collector errors remain; failing sources are not zero. Continue existing attribution reconciliation only.
